name: ACC3b-1-the-glyphs-measured-out-of-the-run
old:
const run = `${lead ? `[${lead}] ` : ''}${marks ? `${n.name} ${marks}` : n.name}`;
      const tw = measureText(font.fnt, run) * s;
new:
const run = `${lead ? `[${lead}] ` : ''}${marks ? `${n.name} ${marks}` : n.name}`;
      const tw = measureText(font.fnt, n.name) * s;
note: The label is centred on the head by subtracting half the run's width, so a run measured without the badge puts every badged peer's name half a badge to the LEFT of their own skull - which is NAME1's entire complaint ("names clip and cut off the top of the sprite head") re-made sideways by the feature meant to decorate it.

name: ACC3b-2-the-title-drawn-on-the-name-line
old: drawText(renderer, font, title.text, Math.round(n.x - tt / 2), Math.round(top - font.fnt.fixedHeight * s), s, title.rgba ?? [1, 1, 1, 1]);
new: drawText(renderer, font, title.text, Math.round(n.x - tt / 2), Math.round(top), s, title.rgba ?? [1, 1, 1, 1]);
note: Mac: "Player titles appear ABOVE a player name." Drawn at the name's own top the two overlap exactly - a title printed through a name, which is unreadable rather than merely misplaced.

name: ACC3b-3-the-party-colour-over-the-title
old: drawText(renderer, font, title.text, Math.round(n.x - tt / 2), Math.round(top - font.fnt.fixedHeight * s), s, title.rgba ?? [1, 1, 1, 1]);
new: drawText(renderer, font, title.text, Math.round(n.x - tt / 2), Math.round(top - font.fnt.fixedHeight * s), s, colorOf?.(n.id) ?? title.rgba ?? [1, 1, 1, 1]);
note: SOC4 owns the NAME's colour and ACC3 does not get a second opinion on it - but the reverse holds too: gold IS the Founder title (Mac named both colours), so a party's green painted over it erases the one distinction the title exists to make. Two labels, two owners.

name: ACC3b-4-the-badge-left-off-the-point
old: title: e.peer.title ?? null, glyphs: Array.isArray(e.peer.glyphs) ? e.peer.glyphs : [],
note: The point is the ONE answer both faces read (ACC1d-MARK's own shape), so a badge that does not ride it is a badge neither face can draw - the whole feature, green everywhere else and invisible on screen.

name: ACC3b-5-the-vocabulary-not-checked-on-the-way-in
old: const title = typeof t === 'string' && TITLES.includes(t) ? t : null;
new: const title = typeof t === 'string' ? t : null;
note: This is a STRANGER'S WORD about themselves - the relay only ever sends what a signature carried, so anything else is a relay that is older, newer, or not ours. Unchecked, a peer's `title` is arbitrary text this client puts on a player's screen in gold.

name: ACC3b-6-the-glyph-run-unbounded
note: With the duplicate check above it the list cannot exceed the vocabulary today, so this looks free - which is exactly the shape of a bound that gets removed - and the campaign confirmed it is unreachable. It is the bound the TOKEN already carries (GLYPHS_MAX in claimsValid), restated at the client's own door, so the two cannot come apart when a third glyph is added.
why: UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION, and the campaign is what proved it rather than an argument made beforehand. The loop above drops any glyph already in `glyphs` and any glyph not in GLYPHS, so the list is a subset of a closed vocabulary and can never be longer than it - and GLYPHS_MAX IS GLYPHS.length, derived rather than picked. No input reaches this line. It stays because it is the bound the TOKEN carries (claimsValid's own check on `g`) restated at the client's door: the day somebody relaxes the duplicate test, or lets GLYPHS_MAX and the vocabulary come apart, this is the line that still holds. A guard whose only job is to survive a change nobody has made yet cannot be killed by a pin, and AUDIT-PW P2 is the standing example of why keeping one is right.

name: ACC3b-7-duplicates-kept
note: A repeated glyph is a relay that got greedy or a body somebody edited, and it draws as a row of identical plants growing off the side of a name.

name: ACC3b-8-the-glyph-order-taken-from-the-wire
note: A glyph is TRUE of a player rather than chosen by one, so two players holding the same glyphs must show them the same way round - and the wire's order is whatever the service happened to build, which is not a promise anybody made.

name: ACC3b-9-a-mark-the-classic-font-cannot-draw
note: ACC1d-MARK's own finding, one slice later and with a shamrock: `drawText` puts NOTHING on screen for a glyph the Daggerfall font has no record for, so the classic face silently drops a badge the DOM face shows - green suite, half a feature.

name: ACC3b-10-the-peer-keeps-the-first-badge-it-was-seen-with
note: A hello is an introduction and the NEWEST one is the true one - the same line already replaces the name and the look. Left out, a player who takes a title off and reconnects goes on wearing it in everybody else's client until they quit, which is the stored-fact trap ACC3a took out of the service reappearing in the client.

name: ACC3b-11-the-remembered-introduction-loses-the-badge
old: this._known.set(id, { name: p.name, title: p.title, glyphs: p.glyphs, lv: p.lv ?? null, sub: p.sub, look: p.look });
new: this._known.set(id, { name: p.name, lv: p.lv ?? null, sub: p.sub, look: p.look });
note: SLAM9's remembered introduction is what stands a peer as themselves across a socket blip - it keeps the name and the look for exactly that reason. Without the badge a blip strips every title in the room until each peer is introduced again.

name: ACC3b-12-the-glyph-run-rebuilt-every-frame
note: "One element per visible peer, MOVED each frame and never rebuilt" is this layer's founding discipline (ui/partyPanel.js: write only what changed). A glyph set changes about twice in a player's life and this runs every frame for every visible peer, so rebuilding it is two DOM elements per peer per frame, forever, for a picture that never changes.
